title: Multimodal approach to preventing suicide in schools project
official: Multimodal Approach to Preventing Suicide in Schools (MAPSS) project: a randomised controlled trial
summary:
Suicide is the leading cause of death in young people under 35 in England. The impact of suicide on a young person’s family, friends, and wider community can be devastating and can also increase their own risk of suicide. The Government guidance for youth suicide prevention programmes does not meet the needs of young people at the moment. There is an urgent need to develop and test suitable ways to prevent suicide in young people.

We plan to deliver a suicide prevention programme in secondary schools across England. This programme, known as the “Multimodal Approach to Preventing Suicide in Schools” (MAPSS), has been tested in six schools in Cheshire and Merseyside with Year 10 pupils (aged 14-15). MAPSS involves delivering a suicide awareness lesson (‘Breaking the Silence’) to all students, then assessing them for suicide risk, and then having an online Cognitive Behavioural Therapy programme (‘Reframe IT-UK’) for students who score at high-risk for suicide.

We have completed a study to test if MAPSS is safe and suitable in the UK with 889 students. Findings showed that MAPSS was safe to deliver, with most students saying they found it useful and would recommend it. Depression, quality of life, and if students may seek help improved for those taking part in the programme. We also found that it would be possible to conduct a larger trial of MAPSS in the UK.

Students and staff reported that suicide prevention should start earlier than Year 10 and that it would be easier to deliver in younger year groups who are not completing GCSEs. For this reason, this next trial will be conducted in Year 9 (13-14 years).
We will carry out a 4-year effectiveness trial in 36 schools. Teachers and parents will complete free training delivered by the suicide prevention charity ‘Papyrus’. Next, schools will be randomly put into two groups. One group will receive the MAPSS intervention (18 schools), and the other will continue with their usual practice only (i.e., control; 18 schools).

Students in MAPSS schools will receive the suicide awareness lesson. Students in all schools will then complete a survey to identify any who may be at high risk of suicide. High risk students in MAPSS schools will be offered Reframe IT-UK, and students in control schools will be offered usual care from their school. All students in MAPSS and control schools will complete surveys before and after the suicide prevention lesson, after Reframe IT-UK, and one-year later, to see whether MAPSS can help reduce suicidal thoughts, improve help-seeking, and increase knowledge, compared to usual practice.

We will also interview students, teachers, and staff leading the suicide prevention lessons to better understand their experiences and views about MAPSS.

Public advisors have been involved in designing this study and will be involved all the time. Three parents with lived experience, the '3 dads walking', and youth clubs supporting young people at risk of suicide are working with us; to make sure that young people’s voices are heard. Young people (aged 14-18 years) have helped with designing study videos, surveys and information sheets. A public representative will be leading and co-ordinating a young people’s advisory group for the study.

We will share our findings in co-developed journal articles, policy evidence briefings, international conferences, tailored reports for parents, children, and education professionals, and videos.
